allocator_prerequisite.cause: A fixed 64-byte transaction allowance rejects a 68-byte system-table counter mutation. Derive the allowance from the actual metadata key and longest encoded signed scalar instead.
allocator_prerequisite.performance_scope: Not a measured optimization and not included in server e2b1853d. No live binary rebuilt after this source-only correctness prerequisite.
allocator_prerequisite.remaining: The analogous sequence counter allowance needs its own regression and root correction; broad Ready not run.

binding_lookup_followup.diagnosis: The global-binding admission check counts all staged keys in the user's transaction rather than committed bindings. Enough unrelated writes enable a per-SELECT binding table reload; clean reads can ignore committed global bindings. Replace the ownership boundary with a node-owned refreshed cache, not a different threshold or a user-session snapshot cache.
binding_lookup_followup.timing_caveat: Session-only switches are diagnostic, not a production optimization. Results stayed equal for all 4096 reads, with 8 warmups discarded from each 128-read batch. Measurements used two serial endpoints and eight alternating on/off rounds; no statistical significance asserted.
binding_lookup_followup.cleanup: Both visibility probes rolled back user-table writes, dropped only their created binding and isolated database. Go owns GC of the normal deleted-binding tombstones.
binding_lookup_followup.planned_validation: Node-owned independent snapshot/cache, session precedence, local write commit publication, peer refresh, failed refresh retention, prepared planning, disabled/deleted/fuzzy binding behavior, and startup/shutdown.
